sentences.text: Shri Aditya Adhikari, learned Senior Counsel assisted by Shr  Tiwari, learned counsel for the petitioner.
Shri Ravikant Patidar, learned Government Advocate for the  respondent/State.

This petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. has been filed by the petitioner to set aside the impugned complaint dated 11.12.2017 and the proceedings under Section 3(1)(zz)(v) and 262)(i) punishable under Section 59 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

It appears that the complainant/respondent being Food Safety Officer seized certain split chana dal (gram) from the possession of Sonu Rajak and Dilip Rajak and on verification it is found that the dal was of sub-standard.
It is submitted that on behalf of the petitioner that Sonu Rajak and Dilip Rajak were neither the employees of the petitioner nor the petitioner had committed any offence.

Moreover, it is further submitted that previously there was a demand by the respondent for some money, which was not satisfied and later on, the complaint has been filed before the Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Satna with ulterior motive.

entities.text:
Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Satna
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: However, according to the submissions, the petitioner is running a society in the name of Pooja Mahila Sva-Sahayata Samuh and there is no such ulterior motive of the petitioner to sell adulterated or substandard goods.
It is further contended that nothing will survive for consideration if the matter is taken for trial, hence, the complaint case be set aside.

In this view of the matter, the petition is allowed and the impugned complaint dated 11.12.2017 and consequential proceeding pending before C.J.M., Satna is hereby set aside on the ground that no material is placed on record showing that Dilip Rajak or Sonu Rajak were acting on behalf the 2 MCRC-3880-2018 petitioner.

(HULUVADI G. RAMESH) JUDGE vkt Smt. Pooja Singh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 27 February, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103291434/
